title: Describing a Place with Relative Clauses

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know relative clauses with *que* and *donde* from B1 Unit 5, and a preposition before *el que* from B1 Unit 20. In this lesson they let you describe the landscape of the south: a cenote, a jungle, an aquifer. When you describe something real, the verb of the relative clause is in the indicative.

sections.title: The relative word you need
rows: una región que tiene muchas selvas
a region that has many jungles (*que* for a thing or a person)
la selva donde viven los jaguares
the jungle where jaguars live (*donde* for a place)
un acuífero del que dependen muchas personas
an aquifer that many people depend on (*depender de* gives *del que*)
los cenotes en los que se puede nadar
the cenotes where you can swim (*en* + *los que*)

items.spanish: Yucatán es una península que no tiene ríos en la superficie.
items.english: Yucatán is a peninsula that has no rivers on the surface.

items.spanish: En Chiapas está la Selva Lacandona, donde viven el jaguar y la guacamaya roja.
items.english: In Chiapas is the Lacandon Jungle, where the jaguar and the scarlet macaw live.

items.spanish: El agua viene de un acuífero del que dependen muchas personas.
items.english: The water comes from an aquifer that many people depend on.

items.spanish: Los mayas visitaban cenotes en los que dejaban ofrendas.
items.english: The Maya visited cenotes where they left offerings.

sections.content: Keep the preposition the verb needs and put it before *el que*, *la que*, *los que* or *las que*, matching the noun: *el acuífero del que dependen*, *la cueva en la que entramos*. Without it the sentence is wrong: not *el acuífero que dependen*.
